newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: Consistent offshore and local exporter dollar selling drove the South African rand to a 5-1/2-week high of 4.5525 bid on the dollar with forex traders optimistic about the unit's short-term outlook.
But technical analysts cautioned that while there could be more strength in the near-term, the longer term bear trend was remained intact.

The rand ended the day more than three cents firmer at 4.5525/5575 on the dollar from 4.5850/5900 at Tuesday's close after an active trading day. In after-hours trade it strengthened further to 4.5475/5525 on the dollar.
Forex traders said offshore banks climbed into the market in early trade selling dollars and local exporters -- mainly mining houses -- joined in the fray.
After rapidly moving to below 4.57 on the dollar, the rand steadied out at the figure towards midday as importers showed a tentative hand and London and European banks took some profits.

Early afternoon trade saw the currency extend its gains, firming to below the 4.56 level to a best intraday level of 4.5525 bid as offshore players and local mining houses continued to offload dollars.
"Dollars flowed in both from exporters and from offshore. The offshore activity appeared bond-related," a senior forex dealer said.
"Players are loathe to run long dollar positions currently," he added.
Another senior trader at a major local bank said hedge fund managers abroad had unwound long dollar positions and this, combined with local exporters had led to the rand's rally.
Darin Grabham, technical analyst at First National Bank, predicted more rand strength in the short-term but said the longer-term picture remained unchanged.

"I think we will see some more rand strength in the near-term with the next target at 4.5370 but we must bear in mind that there's no change in the long-term trend which is still bearish," Grabham said.
The rand also strenghtened on sterling to last trade at 7.6356/6485 from 7.6509/6638 on Tuesday. It was at 0.3344/3349 marks from 0.3326/3332 marks previously.

It was also a cheerful day for local bonds, with the yield on the benchmark R150 bond falling by 17 basis points to an intraday best level of 15.67 percent from a 15.84 percent close on good offshore and local buying, bond traders said.
The R150 broke through key chart points at 15.80 and 15.78 percent in morning trade as the rand strengthened and locals scrambled for stock.
"The move was initiated by locals but the final push though the key 15.80 percent level came from London," one bond trader said.
Bonds yields traded off their best levels above 15.70 percent during the afternoon in what one dealer described as consolidation after "an awful lot of work in the morning."
At 1421 GMT the R150 bond was at 15.71 percent from 15.84 percdent overnight.
Traders said Thursday's trend would be dictated by the rand and the release of third quarter GDP figures at 0900 GMT.
Economists polled by Reuters forecast third quarter GDP to come in at 2.5 percent from 3.5 percent previously with a range of between 1.0 and 3.5 percent.

On the money market, banks quoted their three-month NCD rates unchanged at between 16.95 percent and 17.00 percent offered, while the 90-day BA rate was also steady at between 16.30 and 16.60 percent.
The Reserve Bank indicated the shortage below nine billion rand at 8.974 billion rand on Tuesday from 9.383 billion rand on Monday.
The Bond Exchange said foreigners bought a net 17.20 million rand worth of South African bonds on Tuesday after selling a net 128.74 million rand worth of bonds on Monday.
Nominal cumulative volumes were pegged at 5.86 billion rand on Tuesday from 4.43 billion rand on Monday.
-- Vera von Lieres, Johannesburg newsroom, +27 11 482-1003
